findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SpanFlusher.submit now calls record_stored_segments() only on the freshly constructed per-process SpansBuffer instances in self.buffers, which the consumer's write path never writes through, whereas the old code called it on the single buffer instance shared between the write path and the flusher. If record_stored_segments consumes state accumulated by the write path on the buffer instance (the reason the old flusher held that same instance), no segments are ever recorded for the new buffers, the flusher produces nothing, and spans silently accumulate in Redis until the memory-percentage gate stalls the consumer; note the thread-mode tests share objects with the flusher threads but still not with the write path, so a passing test does not by itself prove the spawn-mode production path.

[ADVISORY] The PR adds the --flusher-processes click option to the consumer definition without touching any code that forwards consumer click params into ProcessSpansStrategyFactory, so the flag only works if that construction site generically passes signature-matching params through. If the factory construction uses an explicit kwargs list, --flusher-processes is silently inert and, because the factory default is None (max_processes falls back to len(buffer.assigned_shards)), production silently flips from one flusher process to one process per shard on deploy, multiplying flusher processes and Redis buffer instances with no flag to control it; this needs a one-minute check of the factory construction site before merge.

[ADVISORY] The added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op lambda at the top (monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)), so the 'Give flusher threads time to process' synchronization never happens. A future reader will assume the sleep provides the synchronization the comment claims and build on it when making the test deterministic, relying on a delay that does not exist; the test currently passes only because step.join() drains the flusher threads, not because of this sleep.

[ADVISORY] The same comma-joined shard identifier is emitted under two different tag keys: 'shard' on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, but 'shards' on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. Dashboards and monitors that group or filter the flusher metrics by the shard dimension silently miss the wait_produce series, and the inconsistency becomes the template for every flusher metric added later.

[ADVISORY] The new _create_process_for_shard method has no caller anywhere in this diff — restarts in _ensure_processes_alive go through _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards) — so it is dead code added by this PR. The next maintainer touching restart logic can reasonably call it expecting per-shard restart semantics that do not exist (it actually restarts the entire process group owning the shard), and its presence obscures that the shard-to-process mapping is fixed at construction time.

[ADVISORY] The flusher process count is unvalidated: --flusher-processes 0 hits the 'max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)' fallback and yields one process per shard, while a negative value passes through min() into range(negative), producing zero flusher processes with no error. An operator setting 0 silently provisions the maximum process count (N flusher processes and N Redis buffer instances instead of 0 or 1), and a negative value silently disables flushing entirely — no process, no health monitoring, no backpressure Values — so spans pile up in Redis until the memory-percentage gate (if enabled) stalls the consumer.

[ADVISORY] In join(), once the deadline expires the for-loop breaks before terminating any process, whereas the old code always terminated the flusher process before returning from a timed-out join. After a timed-out shutdown, join() returns with live flusher processes still producing to Kafka until interpreter-exit daemon cleanup kills them, so shutdown orchestration that assumes join(timeout) leaves no background producers sees a window of post-timeout producing that the previous code did not have.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the actual new behavior — segments from multiple shards multiplexed onto one flusher process being flushed and produced; test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural counts (len(processes), map sizes) and never submits a message, and test_basic runs with the default one-process-per-shard topology. A regression in the shard-to-process round-robin mapping or in the per-subset SpansBuffer flush path (e.g. a subset buffer that never finds its shards' segments) would ship green, and with --flusher-processes set between 2 and the shard count in production some shards would silently stop flushing and spans would accumulate in Redis.

[BUG] flusher_processes is accepted unvalidated: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` maps 0 to the full shard count, and a negative value makes `num_processes` negative so `range(self.num_processes)` yields zero processes and zero buffers. An operator passing --flusher-processes 0 silently gets one process per shard (maximum parallelism, the opposite of the request); passing a negative value creates no flusher processes at all, so submit()'s backpressure loop, memory check, and _ensure_processes_alive all iterate empty collections and the consumer keeps ingesting spans into Redis that are never flushed, silently, until Redis is exhausted.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit is structure-only: it never submits a message and asserts only len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, and a shard total, so the core new behavior — multiple shards sharing one flusher process while all shards still flush correctly — has no behavioral verification. A regression in the shared-process flush path (e.g., the child loop only handling the first shard of its buffer) passes CI and silently defers or drops spans for the co-assigned shards in production.

[ADVISORY] The multiprocessing.Process (spawn) branch is exercised by no test in the diff: both test files construct the flusher with produce_to_pipe set (test_flusher_processes_limit passes produce_to_pipe=messages.append; test_basic asserts `(msg,) = messages`; test_flusher.py asserts `messages`), which forces the threading.Thread branch. The spawn path the ingest-spans CLI consumer actually runs — pickling of the fresh SpansBuffer(shards), cross-process mp_context.Value sharing, and per-process kill/terminate — is unverified; a spawn-only regression (e.g., unpicklable buffer state from a future SpansBuffer change) passes CI and breaks the production consumer at startup.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff drives the health-monitoring restart path: _ensure_processes_alive's kill-and-recreate, the per-process restart counters, and the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError are untested; the only flusher-internals assertion updated here (backpressure_since → process_backpressure_since) shows old-attribute references were migrated, and no restart test existed to migrate. A regression in restart logic (restarting the wrong process index, failing to recreate, or never raising RuntimeError after repeated crashes) surfaces only as unexplained production consumer crashes or permanently stuck shards, not as a CI failure.

[ADVISORY] The added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is inert: the same test's monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) replaces time.sleep module-wide, so the test's own sleep call resolves to the no-op lambda and the synchronization the comment promises never happens. The test remains racy on background-thread timing — on a slow CI worker the flusher thread may not complete its flush iteration before join() sets stopped, intermittently failing the `(msg,) = messages` assertion.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (singular) has no caller anywhere in the diff — construction goes through _create_processes and restarts go through _create_process_for_shards — so this new method is dead code. Future readers must reason about a restart entry point that never executes, and the next change to process creation has two near-identical methods to keep in sync.

[ADVISORY] The same shard dimension is emitted under two different tag keys in the same loop: "shard" on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, but "shards" on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. Dashboards and alerts aggregating flusher latency by shard must query both spellings, and per-shard wait_produce data will not join with produce/segment_size data in any shard-tagged view.

[ADVISORY] In produce_to_pipe (thread) mode, _ensure_processes_alive replaces a hung thread without stopping it — the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard skips kill() for threads — leaving two flusher threads polling and producing the same shards concurrently. After a thread-mode restart triggered by a hung flush (e.g., a blocked Redis call exceeding max-unhealthy-seconds), segments can be flushed and produced to Kafka twice; the old code failed loudly in this path (AttributeError on Thread.kill) rather than duplicating silently.

[ADVISORY] join() breaks out of the process loop once the deadline passes, so processes not yet waited on are neither joined nor terminate()d, whereas the old single-process code always called terminate() after the wait. On a shutdown invoked with a timeout, all flusher processes except the one being waited on when the deadline expires keep running and producing to Kafka until interpreter exit reaps the daemon processes.

[BUG] The new --flusher-processes knob ships with no validation and `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as falsy, so `--flusher-processes 0` silently selects one-process-per-shard while any negative value yields `num_processes < 1`, an empty `process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, and `buffers`, and zero flusher workers. With a negative value the consumer keeps consuming Kafka and writing spans into Redis forever while nothing ever flushes them; the memory-backpressure guard also sums over the empty `self.buffers` (available == 0, so `available > 0` is False), so the built-in safety net never fires and spans are silently lost to Redis TTL expiry.

[BUG] The PR bundles an unrelated CLAUDE.md coding-guideline change (hasattr vs isinstance for union types) that is not traceable to the span-flusher multiprocess work — no code in this diff uses hasattr or introduces union narrowing. A repo-wide coding-policy change rides inside a performance feature PR: flusher reviewers are asked to ratify an unrelated rule, the guideline gets merged on the strength of the flusher work, and reverting either change independently afterwards becomes harder.

[BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test_basic is a no-op: the test's first line, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, patches the same `time` module attribute, so the 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' wait returns immediately. The race the sleep was added to fix is still unfixed — the test's outcome depends on thread scheduling during join()'s busy-wait (whose `time.sleep(0.1)` is also patched to a no-op), so the flake this change was meant to eliminate can still reproduce while the comment claims synchronization.

[BUG] When a flusher thread (the `produce_to_pipe` branch) is detected as hung, the restart path skips `process.kill()` for non-`multiprocessing.Process` objects and unconditionally starts a replacement via `_create_process_for_shards`, leaving the hung thread running alongside its replacement. Two flusher threads then poll the same shards and both produce flushed segments, duplicating span payloads to Kafka and double-emitting the per-shard metrics; in any `produce_to_pipe` deployment a thread stalling past `max-unhealthy-seconds` turns one slow shard group into duplicated output.

[ADVISORY] The factory default `flusher_processes=None` resolves to one process per shard (`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`), contradicting the CLI option's documented default of 1, so the effective default depends on which construction path is used. Any caller that constructs `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` programmatically, or any future consumer definition that reuses the factory without the new click param, silently fans the flusher out to N processes instead of the documented 1, multiplying spawn processes and Redis poll load by shard count with no operator-visible config change.

[ADVISORY] The `buffer: SpansBuffer` parameter injected into `SpanFlusher` is now used only as a carrier for `assigned_shards` (`self.buffer` was removed), while the flusher constructs its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process group, creating a second independent buffer-construction site alongside the factory's. The next change to how the factory configures its buffer (Redis client, batching, compression) will silently not apply to the flusher's buffers, splitting the writer's and flusher's views of the buffer, and maintainers reading the constructor signature will wrongly assume the injected buffer is the one being polled.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) has no call site anywhere in this diff — the restart path calls `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) directly. Dead code: future readers must reason about two near-identically-named creation methods and may wire a future per-shard restart to the wrong one; deleting the method removes the only duplicate entry point.

[ADVISORY] The same shard-identifier value is tagged under two different keys: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards`. Any per-shard dashboard or alert must know both spellings — a query filtering on `shard` silently returns no data for `wait_produce` and vice versa — and adding tags to three previously untagged metric names changes their series identity, staling existing dashboards built on them.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten `_ensure_processes_alive` restart machinery (per-process hang detection, kill, shard-group recreation, per-process restart counting, and the RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS) is not exercised by any test in this diff. A regression in restart handling — recreating a process with the wrong shard set, or never incrementing `process_restarts` so the RuntimeError never fires — would either crash-loop production consumers or leave shard groups with no live flusher indefinitely, and CI would not catch it.

[ADVISORY] Every test in the diff constructs the flusher with `produce_to_pipe` set, so only the `threading.Thread` branch runs; the `mp_context.Process` spawn branch production uses — including pickling the per-shard `SpansBuffer(shards)` and passing `shards` through process args — is never executed, and `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts only constructor state without submitting a single message. A regression confined to the spawn path (a buffer that fails to pickle once restricted to a shard subset, or shards not reaching the child process) ships broken to production while CI stays green, and the core claim of the feature — that spans assigned to a shared process actually get flushed — is never verified end-to-end.

[BUG] submit() now drains stored-segment accounting via `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`, but self.buffers contains only the freshly constructed per-process SpansBuffer instances that never receive store() calls, while the factory-owned buffer that the processing step actually writes segments into is no longer drained (the diff removed the `self.buffer = buffer` reference entirely). The spans.buffer.stored_segments metric silently stops being emitted (drained buffers are permanently empty), and the factory buffer's stored-segments accumulator is never cleared for the lifetime of the consumer process, growing without bound on a hot ingestion path. This is the same dataflow trap as a derived counter maintained by nothing: the write path (store() on the factory buffer) and the drain path (record_stored_segments() on the shard buffers) were split onto different objects by the refactor.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard() is dead code: no call site for it exists anywhere in the diff, and it duplicates the lookup-restart logic already inlined in _ensure_processes_alive(). Future maintainers get a misleading API suggesting a per-shard restart path exists, when the actual restart granularity is the whole process group (all shards sharing that process); the next change to restart logic must be made in two places or the dead twin silently drifts. Passes the deletion test: removing the method changes nothing.

[ADVISORY] In _ensure_processes_alive(), a hung flusher running as a thread (the produce_to_pipe branch) is restarted via _create_process_for_shards() without ever being stopped, because the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips process.kill() for threads. The old thread keeps polling and producing for the same shards while the replacement thread does the same, so two flushers concurrently flush one shard set and emit duplicate Kafka payloads; the shared process_healthy_since Value is also now written by both threads, weakening the hang detection that triggered the restart. Production uses spawn processes (which are killed), so the trigger today is the test/thread path, but the asymmetry between the Process and Thread branches is a latent defect in the shared restart routine.

[ADVISORY] flusher_processes is accepted unvalidated and its falsy/negative values silently change topology: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` maps 0 and None to one-process-per-shard, while a negative value survives the `or` and makes num_processes negative, so `range(self.num_processes)` is empty and zero flusher processes are created. An operator passing --flusher-processes 0 (a plausible attempt to disable the flusher) gets maximum fan-out instead (one spawn process and Redis client pool per shard); passing a negative value silently disables flushing entirely — no process, no backpressure signal, and segments accumulate in Redis until they expire, i.e. silent span data loss with no startup error. The factory default (None → per-shard) also contradicts the CLI help text 'Defaults to 1'.

[ADVISORY] The new metric tags disagree on the key name and value shape for the same dimension: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes are tagged {"shard": "<csv of shard ids>"} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged {"shards": ...}, and flusher_unhealthy (line ~240) tags "shard" with a bare int. Anyone building dashboards or alerts grouped by the shard dimension gets empty series for wait_produce (wrong key) and cannot join flusher_unhealthy's per-shard int tag with the comma-joined string tag on the other metrics; the per-shard incr loop also multiplies one unhealthy event into one metric per shard, inflating series count.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten join() loop `break`s out of the process loop once the deadline has passed, so after waiting on the first (possibly hung) process, all remaining processes are neither joined nor terminate()d — the old code always terminated its flusher process after the deadline. On a shutdown that times out with process 0 hung, processes 1..N keep running and producing to Kafka after join() returns and the committer has stopped, producing segments whose offsets will never be committed; the old single-process invariant 'join always terminates the flusher' is silently lost for every process after the first.

[ADVISORY] Both tests in this diff construct the factory with produce_to_pipe set, so they exercise only the threading.Thread fallback; the production path — mp_context spawn, including pickling the newly constructed SpansBuffer(shards) into the child and the spawn startup of multiple children — is never executed, and no test exercises the multiprocess _ensure_processes_alive restart or the new join() loop. CI stays green while the only code path production runs is unexercised: a pickling failure of the fresh per-shard SpansBuffer (the new constructor usage is exactly the kind of thing that fails only under spawn) or a regression in multi-process health/restart would ship undetected and take down span flushing at deploy time.

[BUG] The new --flusher-processes click option is never forwarded to ProcessSpansStrategyFactory — the parameter is introduced in this diff but no construction site in the diff passes it, so the flag parses and is silently ignored. Operators get no working cap on flusher processes: every ingest-spans consumer runs with flusher_processes=None, which SpanFlusher turns into one spawn process per assigned shard (each a full Python/Sentry interpreter), contradicting the flag's own documented 'Defaults to 1' and multiplying consumer memory/CPU fleet-wide on deploy with no way to revert short of a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] submit() now drives record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() across every freshly-constructed per-shard SpansBuffer retained in self.buffers, although the main buffer the factory already holds provides both, so the parent performs a full Redis memory poll and shard scan once per flusher process instead of once per consumer. The parent process constructs and retains N SpansBuffer instances (each with its own Redis connection pool) at startup and multiplies per-submit Redis round-trips by the flusher process count (which defaults to one per shard given the unwired flag); deleting self.buffers and calling the two methods on the retained main buffer removes both loops and the N extra parent-side Redis clients.

[ADVISORY] Both tests in this diff construct the flusher with produce_to_pipe set (thread mode), so the production spawn path — pickled per-shard SpansBuffer, SpawnProcess startup, and multi-process health/restart handling — is never executed, and test_flusher_processes_limit never submits a message, asserting only structural counts. A regression in the spawn path (e.g., the per-shard SpansBuffer failing to pickle at spawn time or a shared-process flush bug) would ship to the ingest-spans consumer while CI stays green; the shard-sharing behavior this PR exists to deliver has no end-to-end verification.

[BUG] join() breaks out of the process-wait loop when the deadline is already exhausted (next_step.join consumes part of it beforehand), so unlike the old code, which always terminated its process after the wait, no flusher process gets terminate() on a timed shutdown. On graceful shutdown with a timeout, spawn flusher processes are abandoned without SIGTERM and keep polling Redis and producing to Kafka until the parent interpreter exits, extending shutdown and duplicating produce work during supervisor-restart windows.

[ADVISORY] The added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op at its start, so the 'Give flusher threads time to process' synchronization never happens. Whatever race between the current_drift write and the flusher thread motivated this review-iteration change remains unresolved; the test continues to pass or fail on scheduler luck while the comment claims a wait that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The same shard-tag value is emitted under inconsistent tag keys — 'shard' on spans.buffer.flusher.produce but 'shards' on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce — and three previously-untagged series (produce, wait_produce, segment_size_bytes) gain per-process tags. Dashboards or alerts filtering wait_produce by the 'shard' tag return nothing, and the new per-process series change the identity of existing metrics, splitting alert thresholds and SLO queries across old and new series after deploy.

[ADVISORY] max_processes is consumed unvalidated via `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` plus min(), so 0 silently means 'one process per shard' and any negative value yields num_processes <= 0, constructing zero flusher processes. A caller passing a negative flusher_processes gets a consumer that stores spans into Redis with no flusher draining them: submit's backpressure loops iterate empty dicts and the memory check sees available=0, so nothing ever raises MessageRejected and Redis grows unbounded until the shared cluster is exhausted; the new click option (plain type=int, no bounds) accepts such values once wired.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (singular) has no call site anywhere in the diff — restarts in _ensure_processes_alive call _create_process_for_shards directly — making the shard-lookup method dead code. The next change to the restart path has two divergent entry points to reason about, one of them unreachable, and the dead lookup loop silently rots if process_to_shards_map's shape changes; deleting the method removes the ambiguity with no behavioral loss.

[ADVISORY] The PR bundles an unrelated project-coding-convention change (a hasattr-vs-isinstance guideline for union types) into CLAUDE.md alongside the spans flusher work. A project-wide style rule is adopted as a rider on an infrastructure PR whose reviewers are evaluating flusher semantics, so the convention change ships without independent scrutiny or explicit acceptance — a silent expansion of the PR's objective during review iterations.

[BUG] The new --flusher-processes CLI flag (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py, type=int, no validation) flows unvalidated into SpanFlusher where a negative value makes self.num_processes negative, so range(self.num_processes) builds an empty process_to_shards_map and the shard-mapping loop's `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` raises KeyError (since i % -1 == 0 for all i), crashing the ingest-spans consumer at startup. An operator deploying with --flusher-processes -1 gets an immediate consumer startup crash (KeyError: 0) instead of a rejected flag value; additionally --flusher-processes 0 is silently reinterpreted by `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` as one-process-per-shard fan-out rather than the requested cap, spawning more child processes than the operator asked for.

[BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` never sleeps because the same test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 12, so the synchronization the comment promises does not exist. The 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' wait is a no-op; the test passes only because the same monkeypatch makes the flusher thread busy-spin (its own time.sleep(1) is patched out too), so the line misleads readers and any future change that makes the flusher thread actually sleep or drops the monkeypatch exposes the race as an intermittent `(msg,) = messages` unpack failure.

[BUG] `assert total_shards == 4` cannot detect a broken shard-to-process distribution because `process_to_shards_map` pre-initializes every process index with a list, so mapping all 4 shards onto one process (leaving the other with `[]`) still passes every assertion in the test. The comment claims 'Verify shards are distributed across processes' but only the total is checked; a regression in the round-robin assignment (e.g., process_index always 0) ships green — the comment's promise requires asserting the mapping contents (expected `{0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}`).

[ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` never submits a span and asserts no flushed output, so the PR's actual behavior — each process flushing only its assigned shards through its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` view — is never executed by any test in the diff. If the per-shard buffer views don't see the spans the consumer writes, or a process flushes another process's shards (or duplicates them), every test here still passes; checked tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py (test_basic plus this new structural test) and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (only the line-83 backpressure assertion updated) — no test drives a multi-process flusher end to end.

[ADVISORY] The reworked health/restart machinery (per-process `process_healthy_since`/`process_restarts`, the RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per shard group, and the rewritten multi-process `join()`) has no test coverage in this diff. A regression in per-process restart counting or the crash-loop RuntimeError ships undetected; checked tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (only line 83 changed) and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py — neither test kills or hangs a flusher process, so `_ensure_processes_alive`'s unhealthy/restart paths and the new join loop are never triggered.

[BUG] In `join()`, once the deadline expires (including when `self.next_step.join(timeout)` already consumed it), `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop and skips `process.terminate()` for every remaining process, whereas the old code always terminated its process after the wait. During a timed shutdown with two or more flusher processes, a hung process is no longer terminated at the deadline and lingers until the multiprocessing atexit daemon cleanup fires at parent exit; no test in the diff exercises `join()` with a timeout.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) has no caller anywhere in the diff — `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards` — so it is dead code. The method implies a per-shard restart entry point that does not exist; the next reader must trace all call sites to learn it is unused — delete it.

[ADVISORY] The `wait_produce` timer is tagged `{'shards': shard_tag}` while the produce timer (line 185) and `segment_size_bytes` timing (line 195) use `{'shard': shard_tag}` — an inconsistent tag key for the same dimension introduced in the same diff. Dashboards and alerts filtering flusher timings by the `shard` tag silently miss `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`, leaving per-shard produce-wait latency unobservable.

[ADVISORY] Non-positive `flusher_processes` values are unvalidated and untested: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` turns `--flusher-processes=0` into 'one process per shard', and a negative value makes `num_processes = min(negative, N)` <= 0 so `range()` creates zero processes. With zero processes, `process_backpressure_since` is empty so `submit()` can never raise MessageRejected and the memory guard sees `available == 0`, so the consumer keeps draining Kafka into Redis that nothing ever flushes — silent unbounded Redis growth from one bad CLI value.

[BUG] Any negative --flusher-processes value passes the truthy default check and yields num_processes = min(negative, shard_count) < 0, so range() produces zero flusher processes and empty process/process_backpressure_since/buffers maps. With zero flusher processes, submit() never raises MessageRejected (the backpressure loop at line 279 iterates an empty dict) yet still forwards messages to the committer, so Kafka offsets are committed for spans that are never flushed or produced to Kafka — permanent silent span loss with no metric, log, or health signal distinguishing the state (flusher_unhealthy never fires because there are no processes to check); only the optional max-memory-percentage check remains as a stopgap.

[BUG] Passing --flusher-processes 0 hits the falsy-value fallback `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, silently meaning 'one process per shard' instead of the requested maximum of 0. An operator or config-automation script setting 0 (e.g., as a 'disable' sentinel) gets one spawn child per assigned shard — each a full Sentry import with its own Kafka producer and Redis client — exhausting memory/CPU on high-partition assignments and crash-looping the consumer via OOM instead of failing fast on the invalid value.

[BUG] join() breaks out of the shutdown loop when the deadline is exhausted, skipping the process.terminate() call that the previous single-process code always executed after its wait loop. When next_step.join(timeout) or an earlier hung process consumes the join budget, the remaining flusher children — including the hung one — are abandoned without SIGTERM and keep their Kafka producer and Redis connections alive until the parent process exits via daemon cleanup, weakening the shutdown guarantee the old code provided on every timed shutdown.

[ADVISORY] The wait_produce timer is tagged with key 'shards' while the produce timer (line 185) and segment_size_bytes timing (line 195) use key 'shard' for the same comma-joined shard value. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a flusher thread (the `produce_to_pipe` branch) is detected as hung, the restart path skips `process.kill()` for non-`multiprocessing.Process` objects and unconditionally starts a replacement via `_create_process_for_shards`, leaving the hung thread running alongside its replacement. Two flusher threads then poll the same shards and both produce flushed segments, duplicating span payloads to Kafka and double-emitting the per-shard metrics; in any `produce_to_pipe` deployment a thread stalling past `max-unhealthy-seconds` turns one slow shard group into duplicated output.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the restart logic only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; for the `produce_to_pipe` branch `process` is a `threading.Thread` (created in `_create_process_for_shards` when `self.produce_to_pipe is not None`). If such a flusher thread is deemed unhealthy (`cause == "hang"` based on `process_healthy_since`), the code still calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without any mechanism to stop/terminate the existing thread. This can leave the old thread running while a new one is started for the same shard group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The factory default `flusher_processes=None` resolves to one process per shard (`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`), contradicting the CLI option's documented default of 1, so the effective default depends on which construction path is used. Any caller that constructs `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` programmatically, or any future consumer definition that reuses the factory without the new click param, silently fans the flusher out to N processes instead of the documented 1, multiplying spawn processes and Redis poll load by shard count with no operator-visible config change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__` now computes `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, and `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` defaults `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passes it through as `max_processes=self.flusher_processes`. Meanwhile the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is defined with `default=1` and help text “Defaults to 1.” This creates a real inconsistency in defaults depending on construction path, and is a meaningful performance/ops concern, but not a directly provable correctness failure in the diff itself (the CLI path likely passes 1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__(buffer: SpansBuffer, ...)` no longer stores/uses the injected `buffer` instance for flushing; it only uses `buffer.assigned_shards` to compute `self.max_processes`/`process_to_shards_map` and then constructs new per-group buffers via `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`, which are the ones passed into `SpanFlusher.main(...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] submit() now drains stored-segment accounting via `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`, but self.buffers contains only the freshly constructed per-process SpansBuffer instances that never receive store() calls, while the factory-owned buffer that the processing step actually writes segments into is no longer drained (the diff removed the `self.buffer = buffer` reference entirely). The spans.buffer.stored_segments metric silently stops being emitted (drained buffers are permanently empty), and the factory buffer's stored-segments accumulator is never cleared for the lifetime of the consumer process, growing without bound on a hot ingestion path. This is the same dataflow trap as a derived counter maintained by nothing: the write path (store() on the factory buffer) and the drain path (record_stored_segments() on the shard buffers) were split onto different objects by the refactor.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the passed-in `buffer: SpansBuffer` is no longer stored on `self` (the previous `self.buffer = buffer` assignment was removed), and the flusher now constructs new per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances stored in `self.buffers`. In `submit()`, the accounting drain was changed from `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to iterating `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`. The diff does not show any corresponding change that would route the segment `store()`/"stored_segments" increments to these newly created per-process buffers; they are created only for flushing by shard and are not otherwise connected to the producer/write path. As a result, the drain likely runs on buffers that never had stores recorded, while the original buffer instance (the one supplied by the factory) is never drained anymore. This would break/stop emission of the stored-segment accounting and potentially allow the original buffer’s accumulator to grow unbounded if it is still being written to elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In _ensure_processes_alive(), a hung flusher running as a thread (the produce_to_pipe branch) is restarted via _create_process_for_shards() without ever being stopped, because the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips process.kill() for threads. The old thread keeps polling and producing for the same shards while the replacement thread does the same, so two flushers concurrently flush one shard set and emit duplicate Kafka payloads; the shared process_healthy_since Value is also now written by both threads, weakening the hang detection that triggered the restart. Production uses spawn processes (which are killed), so the trigger today is the test/thread path, but the asymmetry between the Process and Thread branches is a latent defect in the shared restart routine.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` the restart path unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` after detecting `cause`, but only attempts to stop the old worker when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (via `process.kill()`). That leaves the original thread still running and polling/producing for the same `shards`, while the new thread does the same, creating a real risk of duplicated flush/produce and also making hang detection unreliable since both threads write to the same `process_healthy_since[process_index]` and `process_backpressure_since[process_index]` Values passed into `main()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] flusher_processes is accepted unvalidated and its falsy/negative values silently change topology: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` maps 0 and None to one-process-per-shard, while a negative value survives the `or` and makes num_processes negative, so `range(self.num_processes)` is empty and zero flusher processes are created. An operator passing --flusher-processes 0 (a plausible attempt to disable the flusher) gets maximum fan-out instead (one spawn process and Redis client pool per shard); passing a negative value silently disables flushing entirely — no process, no backpressure signal, and segments accumulate in Redis until they expire, i.e. silent span data loss with no startup error. The factory default (None → per-shard) also contradicts the CLI help text 'Defaults to 1'.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (new code) treats `0` as falsy, so `--flusher-processes 0` will be interpreted as “use len(assigned_shards)” (one process per shard), which is a surprising topology change and contradicts the intent of a numeric limit. Also, negative values are truthy, so `self.max_processes` can become negative; then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can be negative, leading to invalid setup (e.g., empty `process_to_shards_map` and failure when assigning shards). The diff adds the CLI option without any validation to prevent these cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new metric tags disagree on the key name and value shape for the same dimension: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes are tagged {"shard": "<csv of shard ids>"} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged {"shards": ...}, and flusher_unhealthy (line ~240) tags "shard" with a bare int. Anyone building dashboards or alerts grouped by the shard dimension gets empty series for wait_produce (wrong key) and cannot join flusher_unhealthy's per-shard int tag with the comma-joined string tag on the other metrics; the per-shard incr loop also multiplies one unhealthy event into one metric per shard, inflating series count.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tagging for the same shard dimension: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use key `shard` with a CSV string (`shard_tag`), while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards` (plural). Also, `_ensure_processes_alive` reports `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` in a loop per shard with `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}` where `shard` is a bare int, which won’t match the CSV-string tag shape used elsewhere and multiplies one unhealthy detection into N increments (one per shard). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten join() loop `break`s out of the process loop once the deadline has passed, so after waiting on the first (possibly hung) process, all remaining processes are neither joined nor terminate()d — the old code always terminated its flusher process after the deadline. On a shutdown that times out with process 0 hung, processes 1..N keep running and producing to Kafka after join() returns and the committer has stopped, producing segments whose offsets will never be committed; the old single-process invariant 'join always terminates the flusher' is silently lost for every process after the first.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the new multi-process loop checks the deadline at the top of the `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop and `break`s if `remaining_time <= 0` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py). Because `process.terminate()` is executed only after the per-process wait loop, any processes after the first one are neither waited on nor `terminate()`d once the deadline is exceeded. The old single-process code always ran the `terminate()` block after the timeout loop for the one flusher process. This diff therefore introduces a shutdown path where some flusher processes can remain running after join() returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both tests in this diff construct the factory with produce_to_pipe set, so they exercise only the threading.Thread fallback; the production path — mp_context spawn, including pickling the newly constructed SpansBuffer(shards) into the child and the spawn startup of multiple children — is never executed, and no test exercises the multiprocess _ensure_processes_alive restart or the new join() loop. CI stays green while the only code path production runs is unexercised: a pickling failure of the fresh per-shard SpansBuffer (the new constructor usage is exactly the kind of thing that fails only under spawn) or a regression in multi-process health/restart would ship undetected and take down span flushing at deploy time.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards the execution mode depends on produce_to_pipe: when it is None it uses mp_context.Process (spawn/pickling path), otherwise it uses threading.Thread (target=partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)). In both tests shown/modified, the factory is constructed with produce_to_pipe=messages.append (test_basic already does this, and test_flusher_processes_limit explicitly does), so they only exercise the threading fallback and do not execute the multiprocessing spawn path or validate multi-process lifecycle behaviors like _ensure_processes_alive() restart logic or the multi-process join() loop beyond the thread case. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the click option `--flusher-processes` is added with destination name `flusher_processes` (in `ingest_transactions_options`), and `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` is updated to accept `flusher_processes` and pass it through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] submit() now drives record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() across every freshly-constructed per-shard SpansBuffer retained in self.buffers, although the main buffer the factory already holds provides both, so the parent performs a full Redis memory poll and shard scan once per flusher process instead of once per consumer. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] join() breaks out of the process-wait loop when the deadline is already exhausted (next_step.join consumes part of it beforehand), so unlike the old code, which always terminated its process after the wait, no flusher process gets terminate() on a timed shutdown. On graceful shutdown with a timeout, spawn flusher processes are abandoned without SIGTERM and keep polling Redis and producing to Kafka until the parent interpreter exits, extending shutdown and duplicating produce work during supervisor-restart windows.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff introduces `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` which scans `self.process_to_shards_map` and then calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. Within the shown diff, there is no call site for `_create_process_for_shard`; the restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` dead/unreachable code in the current change, which is a maintainability/clarity issue (two potential restart entry points, one unused) rather than a functional defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new --flusher-processes CLI flag (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py, type=int, no validation) flows unvalidated into SpanFlusher where a negative value makes self.num_processes negative, so range(self.num_processes) builds an empty process_to_shards_map and the shard-mapping loop's `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` raises KeyError (since i % -1 == 0 for all i), crashing the ingest-spans consumer at startup. An operator deploying with --flusher-processes -1 gets an immediate consumer startup crash (KeyError: 0) instead of a rejected flag value; additionally --flusher-processes 0 is silently reinterpreted by `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` as one-process-per-shard fan-out rather than the requested cap, spawning more child processes than the operator asked for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no bounds checking, which is passed through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., flusher_processes=...)` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and becomes `len(...)` (so `--flusher-processes 0` does not cap processes). For negative values (e.g. `-1`), `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative, `range(self.num_processes)` yields an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and the subsequent loop does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` with `process_index = i % self.num_processes` (for `-1`, this is `0`), causing `KeyError: 0` during initialization. This is a concrete crash path introduced/exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` never sleeps because the same test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 12, so the synchronization the comment promises does not exist. The 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' wait is a no-op; the test passes only because the same monkeypatch makes the flusher thread busy-spin (its own time.sleep(1) is patched out too), so the line misleads readers and any future change that makes the flusher thread actually sleep or drops the monkeypatch exposes the race as an intermittent `(msg,) = messages` unpack failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` before the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` call, so that wait is indeed a no-op (and the comment about giving threads time is misleading). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-synchronization issue that could mask races/flakiness, but it’s confined to test behavior rather than a production correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `assert total_shards == 4` cannot detect a broken shard-to-process distribution because `process_to_shards_map` pre-initializes every process index with a list, so mapping all 4 shards onto one process (leaving the other with `[]`) still passes every assertion in the test. The comment claims 'Verify shards are distributed across processes' but only the total is checked; a regression in the round-robin assignment (e.g., process_index always 0) ships green — the comment's promise requires asserting the mapping contents (expected `{0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}`).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly points out a gap in the new test `test_flusher_processes_limit`: it only asserts `total_shards == 4` (sum of list lengths) and does not assert that shards are actually spread across the 2 processes. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `process_to_shards_map` is pre-initialized with empty lists for each process index, so a regression that assigns all shards to one process (leaving another with `[]`) would still satisfy `len(flusher.processes) == 2` (since `_create_processes` creates a process for every map entry) and `total_shards == 4`. This is a test inadequacy rather than a demonstrated product bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` never submits a span and asserts no flushed output, so the PR's actual behavior — each process flushing only its assigned shards through its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` view — is never executed by any test in the diff. If the per-shard buffer views don't see the spans the consumer writes, or a process flushes another process's shards (or duplicates them), every test here still passes; checked tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py (test_basic plus this new structural test) and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (only the line-83 backpressure assertion updated) — no test drives a multi-process flusher end to end.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py) only constructs the strategy with 4 partitions, asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2` and shard distribution via `process_to_shards_map`, then `step.join()`. It never submits any messages/spans into the pipeline and never asserts on produced/flushed output. Meanwhile the core new behavior in `SpanFlusher` is creating per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances in `_create_process_for_shards` and running `main` over those shard-scoped buffers; none of the added/updated tests exercise whether spans written by the consumer are visible to those shard buffers or whether flushing is correctly partitioned across processes. So the finding about missing end-to-end coverage of the new shard/process flushing behavior is grounded in the diff and is not merely generic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reworked health/restart machinery (per-process `process_healthy_since`/`process_restarts`, the RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per shard group, and the rewritten multi-process `join()`) has no test coverage in this diff. A regression in per-process restart counting or the crash-loop RuntimeError ships undetected; checked tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (only line 83 changed) and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py — neither test kills or hangs a flusher process, so `_ensure_processes_alive`'s unhealthy/restart paths and the new join loop are never triggered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new per-process health/restart logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` (per-`process_index` `process_healthy_since`, `process_restarts`, and a new `RuntimeError` when `process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`) plus a rewritten multi-process `join()` that iterates over `self.processes` and conditionally terminates each process. The updated/added tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the one-line change in `test_flusher.py`) only cover basic flushing/backpressure state and process-count/shard distribution; none simulate a dead process (`is_alive() == False`) or an unhealthy hang (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`) to exercise the restart counting or crash-loop `RuntimeError` path. While `step.join()` is called in tests (so `join()` is executed), the failure/restart and hang-handling behaviors are not asserted or triggered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In `join()`, once the deadline expires (including when `self.next_step.join(timeout)` already consumed it), `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop and skips `process.terminate()` for every remaining process, whereas the old code always terminated its process after the wait. During a timed shutdown with two or more flusher processes, a hung process is no longer terminated at the deadline and lingers until the multiprocessing atexit daemon cleanup fires at parent exit; no test in the diff exercises `join()` with a timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the new loop breaks out of the per-process iteration when `remaining_time <= 0` (i.e., deadline reached) before reaching the per-process termination block. Since `process.terminate()` is only called inside the loop after waiting, any processes not yet iterated (or even the first one if `self.next_step.join(timeout)` already consumed the timeout) will not be terminated. The old implementation always called `terminate()` on its single process after the wait, so this is a behavioral regression for timed shutdown with multiple processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Non-positive `flusher_processes` values are unvalidated and untested: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` turns `--flusher-processes=0` into 'one process per shard', and a negative value makes `num_processes = min(negative, N)` <= 0 so `range()` creates zero processes. With zero processes, `process_backpressure_since` is empty so `submit()` can never raise MessageRejected and the memory guard sees `available == 0`, so the consumer keeps draining Kafka into Redis that nothing ever flushes — silent unbounded Redis growth from one bad CLI value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI int option `--flusher-processes` with no validation and threads it into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as “unset” (unexpected), and a negative value is truthy so it is kept. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become negative, making `process_to_shards_map` empty (`range(negative)`), and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will raise (e.g., KeyError) because the map has no keys. So non-positive values are indeed unsafe/unvalidated behavior introduced by this change; the finding’s specific “silent unbounded Redis growth” scenario isn’t fully supported because a negative value will likely crash earlier, but the core defect (no validation leading to broken behavior) is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Any negative --flusher-processes value passes the truthy default check and yields num_processes = min(negative, shard_count) < 0, so range() produces zero flusher processes and empty process/process_backpressure_since/buffers maps. With zero flusher processes, submit() never raises MessageRejected (the backpressure loop at line 279 iterates an empty dict) yet still forwards messages to the committer, so Kafka offsets are committed for spans that are never flushed or produced to Kafka — permanent silent span loss with no metric, log, or health signal distinguishing the state (flusher_unhealthy never fires because there are no processes to check); only the optional max-memory-percentage check remains as a stopgap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does allow a negative `--flusher-processes` through (`click.Option(..., type=int)` has no bounds check), and `SpanFlusher.__init__` uses `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so a negative value remains negative. However, the finding’s downstream behavior is not supported: with assigned shards present, `self.num_processes = min(negative, shard_count)` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is initialized with `range(self.num_processes)` (empty), and then the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and immediately `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which would raise a `KeyError` (since the map is empty), preventing the system from reaching `submit()`/committing offsets. The described “zero flusher processes, submit() never raises, offsets committed, silent span loss” scenario does not follow from the shown code; the more likely outcome is a crash during initialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Passing --flusher-processes 0 hits the falsy-value fallback `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, silently meaning 'one process per shard' instead of the requested maximum of 0. An operator or config-automation script setting 0 (e.g., as a 'disable' sentinel) gets one spawn child per assigned shard — each a full Sentry import with its own Kafka producer and Redis client — exhausting memory/CPU on high-partition assignments and crash-looping the consumer via OOM instead of failing fast on the invalid value.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the diff sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. Since `0` is falsy, passing `--flusher-processes 0` (new click option accepts any `int` with no validation) will be treated as `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, effectively enabling one process per shard rather than respecting the configured limit / failing on invalid 0. This is a real behavior defect directly shown by the added fallback logic and option wiring through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] join() breaks out of the shutdown loop when the deadline is exhausted, skipping the process.terminate() call that the previous single-process code always executed after its wait loop. When next_step.join(timeout) or an earlier hung process consumes the join budget, the remaining flusher children — including the hung one — are abandoned without SIGTERM and keep their Kafka producer and Redis connections alive until the parent process exits via daemon cleanup, weakening the shutdown guarantee the old code provided on every timed shutdown.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the new multi-process loop can `break` out of the outer `for` when `remaining_time <= 0`, which skips waiting/terminating any subsequent flusher processes. In the old single-process code, `terminate()` was always executed after the wait loop regardless of timeout. With the new structure, if `next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting on an earlier process consumes the deadline, later flusher children may be left running without `terminate()` being called.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The wait_produce timer is tagged with key 'shards' while the produce timer (line 185) and segment_size_bytes timing (line 195) use key 'shard' for the same comma-joined shard value. Per-shard dashboards and alerts that correlate spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce with spans.buffer.flusher.produce by shard tag silently miss the wait_produce series because the tag key differs between the two metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff shows `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses a different tag key (`shards`). This inconsistency is verifiable in the diff and would cause metric series to be tagged differently, breaking per-shard correlation/dashboards/alerts that expect a consistent `shard` tag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — no caller exists in this diff, and as a new private method no out-of-tree caller can exist either. Maintainers may assume per-shard restart capability exists and build on it; the method duplicates restart logic that has already drifted in shape from _create_process_for_shards (which keys on process_index, not shard) and should be deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the new private method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is defined but is not called anywhere in the shown diff. Restarts are performed via `_ensure_processes_alive()` which calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and initial startup uses `_create_processes()` -> `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. With no in-file callers and being a new private method, it is effectively dead code and could mislead maintainers about supported per-shard restart behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Per-process state is spread across six parallel dicts keyed by process_index (processes, buffers, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts, process_to_shards_map) that must be kept in sync by hand across __init__, _create_process_for_shards, submit, _ensure_processes_alive, and join. The next per-process field or lifecycle step requires editing every dict and every loop; a single missed site raises KeyError inside submit() on the consumer's main thread and crashes the consumer, and nothing in the structure prevents such a miss — a single FlusherProcess record would collapse the six dicts into one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce multiple per-process dictionaries keyed by `process_index` (`self.processes`, `self.buffers`, `self.process_healthy_since`, `self.process_backpressure_since`, `self.process_restarts`, plus `self.process_to_shards_map`) that are updated/iterated in several places (`__init__`, `_create_process_for_shards`, `_ensure_processes_alive`, `submit`, `join`). This is a real maintainability/robustness concern created by the change: adding a new per-process field or lifecycle action likely requires touching several parallel structures and loops. However, the claimed "single missed site raises KeyError inside submit()" is not directly verifiable as a current defect from the diff, because the dicts are initialized consistently for `range(self.num_processes)` and `_create_process_for_shards` is only called for indices from that map. So it’s not a demonstrable bug right now, but a concrete design risk in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In produce_to_pipe (thread) mode, _ensure_processes_alive detects a hung flusher thread but skips kill() for non-Process objects and starts a replacement thread on the same shards while the hung thread keeps running. The leaked thread and its replacement share the same healthy_since/backpressure_since multiprocessing Values, so the old thread's writes mask the new thread's health signal and both contend over the same shards' flush work; each restart leaks another thread until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS trips and the consumer is restarted.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is deemed unhealthy (`cause == "hang"` based on `process_healthy_since[...]`) it always calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)` to start a replacement, but it only attempts to `kill()` the previous worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. In `produce_to_pipe` mode the worker is a `threading.Thread` (see `_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = threading.Thread` when `produce_to_pipe is not None`), so the hung thread cannot be terminated and is left running while a new thread is started for the same `shards`. Both threads also share the same per-process `mp_context.Value` objects (`process_healthy_since[...]`, `process_backpressure_since[...]`) because those are created once in `__init__` and reused across restarts, so concurrent updates can interfere with health/backpressure signaling while both contend for the same shard flush work. This matches the finding's core issue: restart leaks threads in thread-mode.
